after a long time, I've decided to join the Orthodox Church. I spoke to our parish priest this morning, and we're good to go. What are some resources I should look in to for me and my family to familiarize ourselves with Orthodoxy, coming from Catholicism?

Hello and welcome!

I was born in a mostly Orthodox country so I haven't read a lot of Englih language litereature on the subject. Anyhow, Fr. Seraphim Rose's books were quite enjoyable for me.

On other forums, people praised Kallistos Ware's books The Orthodox Church and The Orthodox Way, so I guess those can be a good place to start. If you come from a Catholic background, I guess that you're familiar with the Church Fathers. If not, then try to find their writings, some of them are considered very important to our faith. As for some post-schism resources, you could try reading about the Hesychast controversy (the dispute between St. Gregory Palamas and Barlaam of Calabria), but be aware that the subject can get pretty complex.

The short stories about the Desert Fathers are always educative and entertaining, so maybe try reading some of those.

If you have questions, it is always better to consult a priest, because laymen (like myself) lack a priest's education on the subject.

This would allow "drunken nights" to happen with bad friends as well as allow veterans who are well coordinated to have an advantage -- albeit it mild.
